name: solve within the span of successive matrix powers of a vector
mechanism: build the subspace spanned by a vector, the matrix times it, the matrix squared times it, and so on, using only matrix-vector products; project the problem onto that growing subspace and solve the small projected problem, whose solution converges to the true one long before the subspace fills the space

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Krylov methods (for large sparse matrix problems; third most-important numerical method class of the 20th century as ran' in section Computational mathematics / Numerical algorithms / Linear algebra:

requires: a matrix-vector product only (matrix need not be stored)
fails_when: the raw powers become nearly parallel; an orthogonalisation step is needed in practice
instances: Krylov methods (for large sparse matrix problems; third most-important numerical method class of the 20th century as ran
